Another money grab by EA, color me surprised. 
Pros:
+NIL is cool
+It's always fun playing a college sports game (unfortunate that EA has a monopoly on the market though)
+Updated rosters, the bare minimum expectation from any sports game
Cons:
-Catch windows are terrible. Hit a receiver in stride, in their hands, and they'll drop it 50% of the time. Not for the CPU though. CPU can have double coverage with a hit-stick primed and make an incredible play.
-CPU gets away with things every play that your players might get away with once in a season.
-Players get caught on each other constantly on mesh routes.
-CPU corners and safeties will reverse on a dime, with their heads turned away from the play to make an interception or break up a pass.
-Running the option and my backs don't even react to the pitch. Or the QB doesn't even release the pitch until he's on the ground and it's a fumble.
-Opposing running backs will bounce off my defensive ends even though there is a 6" and 80lb size mismatch just because they were coded to be GOATs. Conversely my backs get smothered at the line even if they're running behind a blocker. 
-Haven't been able to draw the CPU into offsides/encroachment, but they'll draw someone on my line at least once every game. 

This is only on Varsity difficulty, I tried All-American twice and my line folded like paper every drive even though every metric on my team was better than the oppositions. If you've got a previous year of College Football, just keep playing that one.

Then you're constantly wondering why your 90 overall Stanford offense cannot move the ball on 73 overall Syracuse, or 71 overall Norfolk State, or 69 overall Charlotte...all whilst those offenses are racking it up for 27, 35, 32 points against your 91 overall defense. And so you do some googling, and it says your playbook is bad. So you change your playbook, pick one of the meta ones just because you're tired of watching your team score 6, 10, 13 points - only to watch them score 7, 13, or 17 instead. "But why not play the games?"

Because I'm tired of my RT standing straight up, as if he's just had some glorious revelation, just for the LEDG to bullrush my QB in 1.5 seconds. The blocking logic as a whole, on both sides, so often just leaves free defenders rushing into the backfield, whether the defense is even or undermanned. I'm tired of seeing D-line players jumping to knock down my passes before my QB animation has begun, because they're reacting to the button press. The same issue exists with the DB's, turning around and ball-hawking anything in their area because they know you pressed A, not because your QB is actually throwing it. I'm tired of watching the AI QB always get the ball off right before a sack and it NEVER being a fumble, or a 5'9" 163 lb slot receiver tanking 6 different hit sticks on his way for a 70+ yard touchdown.

And it feels like every player has electromagnets in their shoulderpads. Defenders flashing 7 yards at incredible speeds to catch up for pass breakups, your offensive players just getting stuck like velcro to your own blockers, or you better hope you don't have to run a lot of mesh plays, because your crossing drag routes will spend some very needed time bearhugging in the middle of the field.

The game feels like it hates you, which sucks because this is the only fully fleshed college football game to my knowledge, at least in the legal sense. I will continue to play for that reason alone, and hope it improves, but I'm not having fun.

This game does not feel like football. It feels like you are trying to navigate whatever situation the game says you should be in. Have a superior offensive line? Doesn't matter until the game says it does. Have a scrambling QB? He's slow until the game says he is. Have a dominant defensive line? Well the game wants a close game so they'll have no effect.

When the game was first released, it was actually fun to play. You could run the ball, scheme around defenses and offenses, and really have an impact. Now the game has been messed with via patches that now it just feels like I'm fighting the game to do anything fun.

RTG is still very broken. Dynasty reflects college football now as it is and is a bit overwhelming. I try to trim back transfers and roster changes to make it more manageable, but it does feel like it takes too much time. But I can't fault EA about that. It is unfortunately realistic with the current state of the real game and recruiting.

If you like roster building and doing simulated dynasties, this could be fun for a little bit. But the gameplay itself is just not worth it. For every good play, there are one or two bad ones where it isn't you getting outsmarted or outplayed, but the game deciding you shouldn't win like an offensive tackle not attempting to block the defensive end right in front of them or a wide receiver jumping for a catch to get hit and drop the ball when they could have just ran for a TD.

2.5/10. Wait for a sale near the end of the game's lifecycle to see if they patch it or if the modding community has fixed it.

This game had everything it needed to be one of the best sports games in years. It had the hype, the community, the foundation, and enormous potential. Unfortunately, what should have been a great game has instead become another example of what feels like EA prioritizing profit over quality, innovation, and the community that keeps its games alive.

The most frustrating part is that many of the problems with this game were completely avoidable. It isn't difficult to listen to the community when players are consistently asking for the same features, improvements, and quality-of-life changes. Instead, EA seems to repeatedly make decisions that limit the game's usefulness while creating more opportunities to monetize players. Rather than investing meaningful development time into making existing modes deeper, more functional, and more enjoyable, it feels like content and functionality are intentionally held back so they can be marketed later as features in another title.

The modding community and TeamCrafters have made this even more obvious. Players have demonstrated just how much creativity and potential exists within this game when they are given the tools to do something with it. The community has essentially shown EA what is possible, yet EA continues to restrict what players can actually do within the official game. That makes it difficult not to believe that certain limitations aren't technical impossibilities, but deliberate decisions designed to keep players buying the next game.

One of the most significant examples is Team Builder and Dynasty. Making Dynasty fully functional with offline Team Builder would have greatly enhanced the game's replayability and longevity. This approach could have fostered trust among players and encouraged future purchases. It would have allowed players to create their own teams, build custom conferences and dynasties, and continue enjoying the game without relying on online features. Instead, we're left with restrictions that detract from what could have been one of the game's greatest strengths.

This is what makes the situation so disappointing. EA had the opportunity to create a sports game franchise that could have endured for years of future developments, thanks to its community and customization potential. This commitment could have extended beyond the current game and positively influenced future releases by building trust and ensuring players felt they would receive a high-quality product, rather than a simple rehash with a few extra features. Sadly, it seems the company continues to follow a familiar pattern: releasing a highly anticipated game, making only minimal improvements, monetizing the community whenever possible, withholding useful features, and then using some of those features to promote the next installment.

At this point, I'm honestly glad I bought this game, not because I think it was worth the money, but because it showed me firsthand how EA manages its games and interacts with its community. Watching so much potential get wasted by decisions that seem completely avoidable has taken a lot of the enjoyment out of the game.

This will be the last EA game I buy. I'm tired of supporting a company that seems more interested in maximizing short-term profit than building great games and giving its community the tools it has repeatedly asked for. The community has shown EA what it wants, modders have shown what is possible, and players have continued to support the franchise. The fact that EA still chooses to do the bare minimum with that opportunity says everything.

Players will run up to the ball and stand there, refusing to tackle.  Your defenders will sprint away from their assignment to give the CPU a big play, Your receivers will refuse to run simple routes, your lineman will miss obvious blocks, and your quarterback will throw the ball into the ground two feet in front of him while under no pressure standing still.

If this sounds fun to you, then go ahead.  Just don't expect a football simulation.

If you compare the game to what it COULD be, you will dislike this game very much because it falls well short of its potential.  Why I like the game, however, is that on it's own merit it's a fun game with no real "fatal flaws."  The animations have improved, the gameplay is fun, the AI is reasonably competitive, and it's an immersive experience.

Where EA needs to improve:
1. Customization - allow users to change conference names and rules.  Allow custom playoff formatting.
2. Immersive storylines - the game keeps a lot of data that AI could turn into compelling halftime shows and in-game score updates complete with highlights.  How about partnering with "Locked On" podcasts brand and using AI to generate podcasts for your team, conference, or even national.
3. FCS teams 

My suggestion is that EA goes with the gaming model that the base game is free to play, then keep it updated with "seasons", roster patches, allow creators to mod it, integrate AI for podcasts for a more immersive experience, customization, etc.  Just my opinion.

REVISED: mechanics, game flow, and visual presentation all sit on the extreme end of the spectrum for exquisite gaming. However, like most game, difficulty is just a measure of handicapping the player. This is my first "madden" game is many years, so let me start with my initial impressions:

Wow! Very playable, options on many aspects- play each play or just call plays as the coach. The game flow is very well done, modeling an actual game. Commentary is great, though after a bit is somewhat repetitive- but still helps create a good atmosphere.

After some time at the controller, I could complain about the way the cpu handicaps you, but I think i can still play better; make better passes, call better plays and be more conservative overall. With that this game is challenging and thats not a bad thing. And, if you prefer to play a season where you shutout every team and win the natty in a blowout you can do that too. So there is something for most. 

I can't blame EA or the CPU for intercepting my bad passes. But I can offer this:

-I would buy a DLC of new Commentary.  In the first season this feature is really great, its relevant and colorful. It just gets stale and would be a legit way for EA to increase this franchise revenue.
- I would like the option to simply and completely control the skills of my team. It's a game, if I want to make my QB be able to throw a 90 yard bullet pass, that could be fun.
- coaching points, casual is good but not casual enough. Make a "manual" option- its a game. 
- historical game stat saves. This wonderful great in dynasty. For any game the option to save the game stats would be a another layer of this feature. 
- let off line players save their achievements. This is in the same vein of the microtransactions- THANKS! Just one more ask- you won't lose anything- there's  only a few of us out there..
